newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan import prices rise strongly on weak yen -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan import prices rise strongly on weak yen -- BOJ.

text.p: Japan"s import prices for the first 10 days of February showed a strong rise due to the yen"s weakening, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said on Wednesday.
Data released by the BOJ showed that import prices for the period rose 15.8 percent from February of the previous year.
"The yen has weakened about 16 percent from a year ago. The figure shows that it has been affected greatly by this," the official told Reuters.
But the official said the rise in import prices was not reflected in domestic prices, as domestic supply-and-demand conditions had improved only moderately.
"Although the rise in import prices is putting upward pressure on domestic prices, it has not led directly to higher domestic prices as supply-and-demand has not been that tight," he added.

Domestic wholesale prices for the first 10 days of February rose 0.1 percent from the same period of the previous month, while they dropped 0.2 percent from February of last year, the BOJ data showed.
